blocks.p: Night falls on the Fossoil, and Angel Cross works on. This chapter shows three things that change for the dark: the dashboard of a car, the light of the watch and the colors of the windows.
At night the gauges of the dashboard glow amber. Under the speedometer is a row of lamps; in Figure 14-1 the *HI* lamp is lit.

To light the display of the watch, press *LIGHT* on the full watch. The full watch goes back onto the belt by itself after a few seconds, and opens again when you press the face of the small watch on the belt.
The watch in Figure 14-1 is the digital model described in Chapter 12. Its display gives the day, the date, the time and the air temperature, and its keys are listed in Table 12-1.
The colors of the windows are set from the window menu, as described on the facing page.

caption: Figure 14-1
The dashboard at night, and the watch with its light on.

marks.text: At night the gauges glow amber. The HI lamp is lit.

blocks.p: For the night shift, Angel Cross keeps the Blue accent chosen in Chapter 9 and sets both windows to the Dark theme. Each window has its own window menu, at the right end of its title bar. Figure 14-2 shows the two windows after the change.

caption: Figure 14-2
The Character and World windows at night: the Dark theme with the Blue accent.

blocks.p: To change the theme of a window:

list: Click the window box at the right end of the window's title bar.
Click *Dark*, *Light* or *High contrast*. A check mark shows the theme in use.

blocks.p: The accent is chosen in the same way, under *Accent*.

blocks.note: The *Accent* list, too, has a check mark by the accent in use.

marks.text: Dark theme and blue accent, set from the window menu box.
